html:
Full marks: 100. Time: 2 hours. Choose the best answer. One mark each; no negative marking is reported, so answer every question. How to score yourself: marks = number right. This paper tests different questions, numbers and facts from Model Papers 1 and 2.

This paper's question counts
Group Part Questions
A English (1–40) vocabulary 6, idioms and prepositions 6, articles/tenses/agreement 7, voice/narration/tags 5, clauses/conditionals 6, pronouns/modals 5, reading 5 40
B Mathematics (41–90) arithmetic 10, algebra 10, trigonometry 4, coordinate geometry 7, vectors 2, calculus 7, reasoning 10 50
C GK and IT (91–100) Nepal 3, world 2, computer 3, Internet/programming 2 10

Read the passage and answer questions 36–40.

Ranjana joined the school library only after her teacher asked her to find one fact for a project. She found the fact in ten minutes, but the next hour went on a different shelf, where she opened a book on bridges.

By evening she had decided to study engineering. Her father, a bus conductor, had never been inside a library, and he was surprised that a place with no entry fee could change his daughter's plans.

Later he began to walk to the library with her on Saturdays.

  1. What made Ranjana join the library?aher father's adviceba school rulecher teacher's request to find a factda prize
  2. The next hour she spent reading aboutabridgesbbusesclibrariesdfees

  4. Her father was surprised that a libraryawas so far awaybwith no entry fee could change his daughter's planscwas so largedhad no books
  5. Ranjana's father's work wasabus conductorbengineercteacherdlibrarian

Answer key and explanations

Answers — Group A English (1–40)

1. (c) — obstinate means stubborn.

2. (b) — deep is the opposite of shallow.

3. (d) — omnipresent; omniscient is all-knowing.

4. (a) — vital means essential.

5. (a) — philatelist; a numismatist collects coins.

6. (c) — cheap.

7. (b) — to reveal a secret by accident.

8. (d) — jealous of.

9. (d) — put up with means tolerate.

10. (a) — similar to.

11. (c) — at the last moment.

12. (c) — take after means resemble.

13. (c) — "hour" begins with a vowel sound.

14. (b) — an action in progress when the guests arrived.

15. (a) — "neither of" takes a singular verb.

16. (d) — "now" with "for five years": present perfect continuous.

17. (a) — scissors is plural.

18. (b) — "yesterday" needs the simple past.

19. (c) — "the news" is singular.

20. (b) — present continuous passive.

21. (d) — simple present shifts to simple past.

22. (a) — positive statement, negative tag.

23. (c) — a command becomes told + to.

24. (b) — present perfect passive.

25. (b) — "whom" is the object of "saw".

26. (a) — "were" in the second conditional.

27. (d) — look forward to + -ing.

28. (c) — have/get something done.

29. (b) — "unless you work" = if you do not work.

30. (d) — let + bare verb.

31. (a) — "little patience" has a negative sense.

32. (b) — junior to.

33. (d) — scarcely … when.

34. (c) — obligation: must.

35. (b) — "each of the boys" + singular verb.

36. (c) — "only after her teacher asked her".

37. (a) — "a book on bridges".

38. (d) — "decided to study engineering".

39. (b) — "a place with no entry fee could change his daughter's plans".

40. (a) — "a bus conductor".

Score sheet and error analysis

Use the figures and steps below after you finish the paper. Mark your sheet with the answer key, enter the group scores, then work through the error log.

  1. Score each group separately and compare with the target boxes in Fig 4.2. A low group tells you which units to revisit first.
  2. Write an error log line for every miss: question number, the cause (formula, arithmetic slip, grammar rule, never learnt) and the unit that fixes it.
  3. Redo each missed question after two days, without looking at the explanation. A question you can now solve is fixed; one you cannot goes back into the log.
  4. Check your time: if Mathematics took more than 70 minutes, practise skipping and returning (Fig 4.2).
  5. Do not read patterns into the key (Fig 4.1). The letters are spread across a, b, c and d.
